title: Israeli strikes kill eight people in Gaza - medics say
gist: Israeli strikes killed at least eight Palestinians in Gaza, including five police officers, as Israel steps up attacks it says target Hamas rearming in violation of a year-old ceasefire. Reconstruction is stalled because talks on Hamas disarmament and Israeli withdrawal have failed, with Israeli troops controlling about two-thirds of the territory.

insights.claim: Israeli strikes on Nov. 1, 2026 killed at least eight Palestinians in Gaza, including five police officers in western Khan Younis.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Ongoing strikes show the ceasefire is fragile, sustaining regional risk.

insights.claim: Israel has stepped up strikes in recent weeks, saying Hamas is rearming and launching attacks in violation of the year-old ceasefire, which Hamas denies.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Escalation trend raises odds of ceasefire collapse.
insights.locator: Israel, which says the Hamas militant group

insights.claim: At least 1,500 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza since the ceasefire according to local health officials, while Israel says four soldiers have been killed.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: The ceasefire has not stopped substantial violence, limiting normalization and reconstruction momentum.
insights.locator: At least 1,500 Palestinians have been killed

insights.claim: The US-brokered Gaza ceasefire calls for eventual reconstruction, but little progress has been made because negotiators have failed to agree terms for Hamas disarmament or Israeli troop withdrawal.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Reconstruction-related opportunities (construction, materials, Gulf funding) remain on hold until the disarmament/withdrawal deadlock breaks.

insights.claim: Israeli troops control about two-thirds of Gaza, and nearly all of its more than 2 million residents live in the remaining third, mostly in tents and damaged buildings under effective Hamas control.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: De facto partition entrenches a humanitarian crisis and long-run instability.
insights.locator: Nearly all of the more than 2 million residents
